purpose: Define the migration and acceptance evidence required before and during implementation without authorizing or inventing physical schema.
migration_evidence: Every shared schema change must be represented by a new immutable ordered migration under the governed migration path.
Empty-database migration replay must deterministically produce the intended schema.
No direct schema synchronization or manual production DDL is permitted.
Production migration execution remains separately gated by unresolved C21 backup/restore policy; this plan does not authorize production execution.
acceptance_evidence: Static persistence-admission test rejects schema definitions that encode candidate or unapproved semantic dependencies.
Reconciliation persistence test proves an OPEN record with unreadable provider state remains unresolved and cannot authorize retry.
Idempotency test proves same-key/same-payload retry does not create a duplicate authoritative effect.
Key-reuse negative test proves an idempotency key cannot be reused across operations or with a different payload.
Scope negative test proves ReconciliationRecord scope cannot broaden beyond the originating operation's authoritative scope.
Repository-boundary test proves TransactionControl owns writes to ReconciliationRecord persistence and foreign modules cannot write it directly.
Migration replay evidence and the relevant TransactionControl acceptance tests must be attached to the implementation PR before physical-slice completion.
